responses.response: Use this pre-commit checklist: 1) Kinds: confirm the new worker uses a container kind that exists in `projects/shared/spec-containers.c4`; for a background processor, sanity-check whether `Container_ProcessingServer` or `Container_Webapp` better matches its role. 2) FQNs: trace every reference to the worker in model, views, and any `instanceOf`-style usages and make sure the same system-qualified path is used everywhere; the shared examples use container FQNs like `vault.api`, so your worker should follow one consistent pattern with no stale names. 3) Relationships: verify each edge uses a shared relationship from `projects/shared/spec-global.c4` (`calls`, `async`, `reads`, `writes`, `uses`) and that the label plus technology still match the behavior; `SPEC_CHEATSHEET.md` says to keep the interaction technology on the system-model relationship. 4) View scope: in the dedicated C2 view, only the relevant actor and `#Container` elements should appear; if anything rendered as a `#Component`, the scope is wrong for C2. 5) Rendering: render the view and check that the worker shows the expected icon/shape for its kind, synchronous links stay solid blue, async links stay dashed blue, and there are no orphaned, duplicated, or unexpectedly inherited elements.

In a C2 detail view, validate the parent context by checking the included set, not just the parser result: the user should be one of the actor kinds from `projects/shared/spec-context.c4`, the web application and API should be container kinds from `projects/shared/spec-containers.c4`, and nothing from `projects/shared/spec-components.c4` should sneak in. Then inspect each include rule and ask what else it can match: exact FQNs are safest, while broad filters such as all `#Container` elements are risky because every container kind carries that tag. A quick sanity test is that every included container should share the same system prefix in its FQN, while the user sits outside that system boundary. If the rule could also pull sibling containers, other APIs, or any component-level element, the parent context is too broad.

Treat this as a semantic review, not a syntax review. In `projects/shared/spec-global.c4`, `calls` and `async` are both valid, but `async` specifically means asynchronous messaging and renders as a dashed blue line; `SPEC_CHEATSHEET.md` pairs it with queue-style behavior and technology such as `AMQP`, while synchronous examples use request/response semantics. To validate the model, check four things: the interaction is truly fire-and-forget or message-driven; the relationship label still describes async behavior rather than a blocking call; the technology value still fits async semantics; and the topology still makes architectural sense. If the edge is now a direct async link between two ordinary containers and the C2 view looks odd, that is a strong hint that a `Container_Queue` should probably exist explicitly between them instead of hiding the broker. If the rendered dashed line is accepted by LikeC4 but makes the dependency story less believable, the model is syntactically valid but semantically weak.
